title: Jonah and the Contact
premise: Noor Galloway, a fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map — discovers her own safe house listed for sale online, its interiors photographed by someone who knew every room. The listing is a message from the network that trained her: the same people who rewrote her identity twenty years ago are now selling the people they built, one asset at a time, ahead of a summit where their buyers will convene. As Noor traces the listing through a chain of burned colleagues and a teenage hacker who becomes her unlikely family, she learns the Office itself authorized the sale — her loyalty was always the product. In the end she detonates the network from inside the summit itself, choosing truth over the institution, and walks away with the found family she built rather than the identity she was given.
about_author: Petra Oyelaran is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian missions who writes thrillers about the people institutions forget to count. She lives between Lagos and Lisbon, and claims her best plot ideas arrive on overnight flights.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Scrolling property sites at 2 a.m., Noor finds her safe house for sale — every room photographed, including the wall safe she installed herself. The agent's name belongs to a man she buried in 2009. Beat: cold dread; the life she curated is now merchandise.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. She reports the listing to the Office and receives a routine order: stand down, change addresses, say nothing. The obedience is automatic — and that automaticness frightens her. Beat: unease beneath competence; the rules are rewriting themselves again.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Watched the House
chapters.summary: POV: Teo, sixteen, a hacker who cased the property for the listing and kept copies he shouldn't have. He contacts Noor anonymously, terrified, offering the raw files for money. Beat: wary transaction; two loners circling the same secret.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. A rare summons to the Office's real headquarters. Her handler, Voss, praises her discretion and mentions the summit — six weeks out — and a 'portfolio review' of long-serving assets. Beat: flattered and chilled in equal measure; praise as a leash.

chapters.title: Photos of the Inside
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Teo decodes the listing's metadata: the photos were taken over three years, from cameras Noor never found. Whoever shot them lived with her. Beat: violation; intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: The Widow of Room 4
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Noor visits Ada, widow of a former asset, and finds the same listing format on Ada's late husband's flat — sold last month to a shell buyer. Ada remembers Noor from a life Noor was trained to forget. Beat: grief and recognition; the network's pattern emerges.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. One of the photographed assets, Callum, is found dead in a canal, ruled accidental. The Office sends Noor to 'assist' the cover story. She writes the lie in her own hand. Beat: complicity; loyalty starting to taste like ash.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Teo, now hunted by someone sweeping up loose metadata, breaks his own protocols and shows up at Noor's new address. She should turn him away. She doesn't. Beat: reluctant shelter; found family begins as an inconvenience.

chapters.title: The Curriculum
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Teo's files reveal a training program — 'the Curriculum' — that manufactured identities for assets, including Noor's own origin file, sealed and priced. Her name is a lot number. Beat: identity shattered; the past becomes inventory.

chapters.title: Voss's Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Noor realizes the interior photos were shot from Voss's vantage — he visited the safe house for years under maintenance pretenses. Confronting him means confessing she looked. Beat: paranoia sharpened into certainty; the hunter is the handler.

chapters.title: Everything Must Go
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Teo finds a dark-web catalog: eleven assets, photos, dossiers, reserve prices. Sale closes the night before the summit. Two listings are already marked SOLD — one is Noor. Beat: horror; she isn't investigating the network, she's in the window display.

chapters.title: Ada's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Ada, before dying quietly in her sleep, mails Noor a ledger of every asset the Curriculum processed — including three still active inside the summit's security detail. Beat: inheritance of truth; the dead recruit the living.

chapters.title: The Rules of Lying
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Noor feeds the Office a flawless false report to buy time, using every technique the Curriculum taught her. She is excellent at it and hates herself for it. Beat: the trained liar turned against her trainers; loyalty and truth pull apart.

chapters.title: Middle of the Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. The sweepers trace Teo; Noor extracts him mid-abduction in a scene that blows her own cover. They flee to the condemned original safe house — the one for sale. Beat: the cost of caring; family chosen under fire.

chapters.title: Inside the Walls
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Hiding in her own former safe house, Noor finds the camera nest and, behind it, a complete duplicate of her file — with a handwritten annotation in Voss's script: 'best build yet. hold for summit.' Beat: rage with nowhere to put it; she was the prototype of the sale.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV: Noor and Teo, alternating. They plan: reach the summit, expose the catalog to the buyers themselves, and burn the network's credibility in front of its market. Each makes a private contingency the other doesn't know about. Beat: grim resolve; love expressed as tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Noor makes contact with the buyer who purchased her listing — a rival service that will pay her to defect with the Curriculum's master keys. The offer is everything she's earned and everything she despises. Beat: temptation; the exit ramp is paved with the same stone.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Teo infiltrates the venue's systems while Noor walks in through the front, badged, unremarkable, exactly as built. Voss greets her warmly. Beat: dread at the threshold; the mask fits too well.

chapters.title: Portfolio Review
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. In the summit's back rooms, Voss reveals the sale was a loyalty test and offers Noor partnership — run the Curriculum, protect the family that made her. He genuinely believes it's love. Beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth; she sees her future offered as a gift.

chapters.title: Everything Must Burn
chapters.summary: POV: Noor and Teo. Noor says yes — and uses her new access to dump the entire catalog, dossiers and reserve prices, onto every screen at the summit. Buyers scatter, the network's market collapses in real time, and Voss understands too late. Beat: climax; truth detonated in the temple of the deal.

chapters.title: After the Sale
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. In the aftermath, the Office disavows the Curriculum and offers Noor a clean new identity — the twentieth rewrite. She declines, keeping the name she chose for herself. Beat: quiet aftermath; identity reclaimed as authorship, not assignment.

chapters.title: For Sale by Owner
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Months later, Noor and Teo — plus Ada's orphaned grandson — share a shabby flat with too many locks and one good kitchen. Noor posts her own listing online: the old safe house, photos of the inside, sold honestly at last. Beat: resolution and warmth; the family that chose itself closes the door gently.
